introduction: Colorado Works is the state’s TANF program for eligible families. It combines cash assistance with case management, education, training and employment support.
description: Colorado Works is the state’s TANF program for eligible families. It combines cash assistance with case management, education, training and employment support.

sections.who: Families with children, some caregivers and pregnant applicants can apply. Colorado residency, qualifying status and financial rules apply. Your county makes the eligibility decision; a general screening statement is not a guaranteed award.
sections.get: Cash can be delivered by EBT or direct deposit. A case manager helps build a Colorado Works Journey plan around family and employment goals.
sections.docs:
• Identification and household members’ information.
  • Income and relevant family or pregnancy records.
  • Contact details and information about barriers to education, training or work.
sections.apply:
1. Choose an application option

    Use PEAK, MyCOBenefits or a paper application linked from Colorado Works.

  2. Work with your county

    Respond to requests for verification. The county human or social services office can help with the application.

  3. Plan the next steps

    If approved, discuss goals and supportive services with the case manager. Ask how payment will be delivered and what participation requirements apply.
sections.after: Keep appointments and case notices. Report changes as directed and tell the case manager about difficulties that affect participation.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Colorado Works overview and application. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Can a caregiver apply for a child?
The state says some children not living with their parents can participate; ask the county about your arrangement.
Is this only a cash payment?
No. Colorado Works also offers case management and education, training and employment support.
